judgePersona: Senior engineer who debugs mirage agents daily, lives in /replay payloads, and needs the "model mistake vs data mistake?" verdict in seconds. Impatient with chrome, ceremony, page-shuffling, and anything that makes me re-find my place. I trust solid/muted/dimmed honesty tiers because I've been burned by dashboards that fake provenance. I verified the data layer myself: ReplayAction is 12-fielded with tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision/is_cache, the stateAt fold is real, touched-by is a client-side join with NO server endpoint, and the fake tables (users/invoices/subscriptions/events) ship real schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json. I reward designs that get me from a flagged run to the offending byte (and back) in one click, and I punish designs that make me arrange furniture before I can debug.

rankings.notes: This is the one that respects my time. ONE shell that never changes shape, center swaps exactly one object (Run or Data), lenses re-skin over a SHARED ?cursor so I never lose the op I'm staring at. The two-tree left rail (Run History top, Data Catalog bottom) puts both worlds side-by-side permanently, so the model-vs-data pivot is literally a glance: [open in Data ↗] from any VfsOp leaf lights the touched-by card; a touched-by row jumps me back into Time-Travel at the exact idx with the op ringed. That bidirectional bridge is THE feature and it's the tightest here. The decisive intellectual move — both the run's Profile-tree leaf and the data object's lineage card are the IDENTICAL mount_prefix+path join read two ways — is the cleanest articulation of why it's one product, not two. Honesty is drawn in pixels with a hard boundary (solid=observed byte from /replay, muted=derived is_cache/self-reported intent/client column profiles, dimmed=not-yet-emitted), which I verified maps exactly to what the store returns. Data View is genuinely Snowsight-grade: 13 real mounts, database mount wears a full table skin (schema grid + FK row labeled 'declared, not observed dataflow' + virtualized data.jsonl with per-column client-side profiling), disabled query bar with explicit NotImplementedError. INTENT+COMMAND card is the directive-1 grain done right: Step(intent)->[ToolCall(command)->VfsOp(effect)], collapsible (not rigid 1:1), with the conservative INTENT!=EFFECT amber flag that only fires when self-reported 'live' meets is_cache=true or path-A-said/path-B-read — that flag IS my fast triage. Buildability docked 2: the two-tree-rail + center-swap risks reading as two apps if the cross-links aren't instant (their own #1 risk), and 'Most Expensive Ops -> ring node + snap cursor' across Profile/Time-Travel needs the shared selection wired carefully. But every primitive (consoleStore, RunTracePanel, OverlayDiff, getReplay, vfsList) already exists. Lineage-as-a-lens (not a nav item) is exactly correct and matches that there's no lineage endpoint. Best learnability of the three: if you've used Snowsight, you already know this — zero dock vocabulary to learn.

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — Paradigm C: The Trace Debugger
rankings.notes: My instinctive favorite emotionally — 'a run is a recording you scrub' is exactly how I think, and the debugger organism (LEFT spine / CENTER lens-stage / RIGHT docked inspector / BOTTOM transport, all bound to ONE cursor) is the purest Redux-DevTools translation. The inspector's causality crumb ('dispatched from' run>step>tool_call>this op, each segment clickable) is the single best inspector design across all three — it re-states the selected op as a permanent anchor so switching PROFILE/TIME-TRAVEL/LINEAGE never disorients me, directly answering its own learnability risk. Lands you at cursor=last (final state, scrub backward) — correct Redux mental model and matches the server defaulting cursor to total-1. Time-Travel DIFF-default showing the intent+command card ABOVE the exact state.diff is the right altitude. Data View is co-equal with Snowsight Console (same 13 mounts, table skin, disabled query bar, client-side column profiling, touched-by panel with the honest 'op-level, this workspace's loaded runs, not a transitive provenance graph' footer and dimmed [graph] preview). The JOIN IMPLEMENTATION NOTE explicitly states there's no /api/lineage and the join is client-side — most honest of the three about the exact thing I verified. Data wiring section correctly names the live useAgentStream lossiness (drops tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision) and routes the debugger exclusively through /replay+getSessionTrace. Why it lands just under Snowsight Console for ME: it's route-driven ([Home][Data] nav switch, /runs /data /compare routes) where Snowsight Console is object-swap-in-one-canvas — the routing means Run and Data are sequential surfaces ('back to run' pill) rather than simultaneously visible, so the model-vs-data pivot costs a context switch instead of a glance. The four-region-plus-four-deep-card-disclosure-plus-transport is a LOT of chrome (its own risk #8); denser to learn than the Snowsight metaphor. Buildability equal to Snowsight Console — same real primitives, slightly more surface (full routing + 4 regions). Functionally near-identical to Snowsight Console; it loses only on simultaneity and learnability.

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — The Workbench (Paradigm B: IDE Workbench)
rankings.notes: The most powerful ceiling and the worst fit for an IMPATIENT debugger. The CROSS-FILTER CONTRACT (every pane subscribes to one {workspaceId,branch,runId,opIdx,path} store; set opIdx anywhere and Inspector/State/Data/Lineage/Profile/transport all re-bind) is the most elegant articulation of 'one shared selection' and is genuinely the soul of what makes any of these feel like one product — this idea should be GRAFTED into the winner. Docking two lenses side-by-side over one cursor (scrub Time-Travel left, watch Most-Expensive-Ops re-rank right) is a real power-user payoff. Data View and intent+command card are co-equal best-in-class. But the VS-Code-dockable-panes paradigm fails my core requirement: I want the answer in seconds, and this design makes me ARRANGE FURNITURE first. Yes there are Triage/Debug/Catalog presets, but the whole pitch is 'the workspace is a project you live inside' with draggable splits, ⌘\, persisted layouts — that's a tax for someone who just wants to see if a run read a stale cached path. Their OWN risk #1 admits users may never discover panes are dockable. Learnability is the lowest of the three by a wide margin (dock vocabulary, split semantics, layout presets). Buildability is also lowest: a real tab-and-split dock manager with drag/resize/persist is substantially more frontend engineering than 'swap the center object' (Snowsight Console) or 'route to a 4-region debugger' (Trace Debugger), and the cross-filter fetch-storm risk (every opIdx change re-requests /replay) forces a client-side _fold_replay_state port to be done correctly up front. Same real data primitives as the others, but the shell itself is the expensive part. For a senior eng debugging daily this is the right SUBSTRATE (shared selection) wrapped in the wrong UX (dock manager).

bestIdeasToGraft: From Paradigm B (Workbench): the CROSS-FILTER CONTRACT as the explicit architectural spine — ONE selection store {workspaceId,branch,runId,opIdx,path}; setting opIdx anywhere triggers the stateAt(idx) re-fold and ripples to every surface (inspector swaps to that VfsOp, Data lights cursor_op.path, Lineage recomputes touched-by, transport snaps); hover=faint cross-highlight, click=committed ring. This is the engineering substrate that makes Snowsight Console's 'one shell' illusion actually hold.

From the Trace Debugger (C): the docked inspector's CAUSALITY CRUMB header — 'dispatched from' run>step>tool_call>this op with each segment clickable, re-stating the selected op as a PERMANENT anchor chip that never changes across lens switches. This single element kills the #1 learnability risk (users not realizing lens-switch keeps the same op) better than anything in the winning design.

From the Trace Debugger (C): the explicit JOIN IMPLEMENTATION NOTE / honesty footer pattern stating in-product that there is no /api/lineage and touched-by is a client-side mount_prefix+path union over THIS workspace's loaded runs — verified accurate against the codebase. Make this caption load-bearing and unmissable on every lineage panel.
From the Trace Debugger (C): land the run at cursor=last (final state, scrub backward) — the correct Redux mental model and it matches the server defaulting cursor to total-1.

From Paradigm B (Workbench): the optional 'dock two lenses over one cursor' as a power-user ESCAPE HATCH (e.g. ⌘\ to split Profile beside Time-Travel) — keep it opt-in and hidden by default so it doesn't tax newcomers, but offer it for the scrub-left/watch-cost-re-rank-right workflow.

From Paradigm B (Workbench): client-side stateAt(idx) re-fold (port _fold_replay_state) for scrubbing — request /replay once per run, fold locally on cursor moves, only re-request on run change. Essential to avoid a fetch-storm and to keep scrubbing instant; the server fold stays the source of truth (pure function, provably identical).

Universal across all three (keep verbatim): INTENT+COMMAND card grain Step(intent)->[ToolCall(command)->VfsOp(effect)], collapsible not rigid 1:1, with the CONSERVATIVE INTENT!=EFFECT amber flag that fires ONLY when self-reported intent exists and contradicts the observed op (says live/latest but is_cache=true, or names path A but read path B), never on absent intent, always labeled 'possible mismatch — heuristic, not a verdict'. The intent row is muted (self-reported via AG-UI THINKING) and reserves the exact slot to flip to a solid 'observed intent' chip with zero layout change when a cognition plane lands.

Universal: the disabled query bar with explicit NotImplementedError tooltip + 'derived from files / column profile computed client-side / no live SQL' captions, and NEVER zero-filling fingerprint/revision on disk mounts (show '—', S3-only via ETag). All three nailed this; it must survive synthesis.
synthesisAdvice: Ship Snowsight Console's SHELL and Trace Debugger's INSPECTOR on top of the Workbench's STORE. Concretely: (1) Keep Snowsight Console's exact composition — one persistent three-region shell (44px context bar with workspace/branch chip + breadcrumb + Cmd-K; 300px left rail holding the two trees Run History over Data Catalog; fluid center that swaps exactly ONE object, Run or Data). Do NOT adopt the Workbench's dockable-pane manager — it's the wrong UX for an impatient debugger and the most expensive thing to build. Do NOT adopt the Trace Debugger's separate /data and /runs routes either — the object-swap-in-one-canvas is what makes the model-vs-data pivot a glance instead of a context switch; that simultaneity is the whole product. (2) Underneath, implement the Workbench's cross-filter contract literally: a single {workspaceId,branch,runId,opIdx,path} store where setting opIdx folds stateAt(idx) CLIENT-SIDE (port _fold_replay_state; fetch /replay once per run) and ripples to the center, the inspector, and the left-rail highlight. This store is what upgrades Snowsight Console's 'shared ?cursor' from a permalink into a live nervous system and directly defuses its top risk ('reads as two apps'). (3) Replace Snowsight Console's right-inspector header with the Trace Debugger's clickable causality crumb + permanent selected-op anchor chip — this single graft neutralizes the lens-disorientation risk for free. (4) Lenses stay as a segmented strip that re-skins the center over the shared cursor (Snowsight Console), with the Workbench's ⌘\\ split-a-second-lens as a hidden power-user opt-in only. (5) Carry through, non-negotiable and verified against the code: solid/muted/dimmed honesty tiers baked into shared primitives (border-style + opacity + chip, never per-screen); touched-by labeled 'this workspace's loaded runs, not provenance' on EVERY panel with the Trace Debugger's explicit no-/api/lineage note; disabled query bar with NotImplementedError; never fake fingerprint/revision on disk mounts (show '—'); reads_so_far rendered 'paths only — no per-read bytes' (the store really is string[]). (6) The INTENT+COMMAND card with the conservative INTENT!=EFFECT flag is the run-inspection grain in all three — keep it identical, and surface the flag as a column on the Home run table so triage starts before I even open a run. Net: Snowsight learnability, Redux inspector clarity, Workbench cross-filter wiring — minus the dock-manager build cost and the route-induced context switches. That gives me the model-vs-data verdict in seconds.

judgePersona: Daily Snowflake/Databricks power user with strong taste for data catalogs, query profiles, and lineage tabs. I live in Snowsight's database explorer and Query Profile, and in Databricks' lineage tab. I judge whether the Data View feels like a real catalog + results auto-profiling, whether Profile feels like a real operator tree with Most Expensive Nodes, and whether Lineage is honest about being op-level rather than faking a provenance graph. I verified the designs' claims against the actual repo: the 13-field ReplayAction + stateAt fold (_fold_replay_state, pure, returns full actions[]), the real schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json fake tables (users: 500 rows / 105,590 bytes / 2026-05-15, real FK account_id->subscriptions.account_id), _console_mounts_detail (prefix/resource/mode/effect_class), and the reusable components (RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow/ReasoningBlock, OverlayDiff, EffectClassTag/CaptureBadge/mountColor, SegmentedControl, EmptyState). The touched-by join is client-side over get_vfs_ops (no server lineage endpoint) — all three designs state this honestly.

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — Paradigm C: "The Trace Debugger"
rankings.notes: As a Snowsight/Databricks user, this is the spec I'd hand an engineer and trust. Review-loop fit (9): the debugger-organism (LEFT spine / CENTER lens-stage / RIGHT docked inspector / BOTTOM transport, all on ONE cursor) is the exact 'open a recording and scrub it' motion that beats re-running; the persistent 'selected op' anchor chip across lenses (its own mitigation for lens-confusion) is the right call. Data View (9): the most Snowsight-COMPLETE of the three — catalog tree with effect-class dots + reversibility tooltips, table skin with the REAL stats strip (I verified users=500/105,590B/2026-05-15 against the fixture), DISABLED query bar with explicit NotImplementedError tooltip, Schema grid + FK row correctly labeled 'declared schema, not observed dataflow' (the FK genuinely exists in schema.json), virtualized data.jsonl with per-header mini-profiles, and a right column with client-side column profiling (top-values for plan/status, histogram for created_at/last_login — exactly matching the real column types) + the touched-by panel with op-type/source facets and an honest footer. It even shows table-level stats.json SOLID next to MUTED client-derived per-column stats so the authoritative numbers are never confused with derived ones — that is precisely the distinction a profile-literate user cares about. Intent+command (9): the clearest card spec — collapsed default with one intent row + repeating command/effect, the conservative INTENT≠EFFECT flag ('live' vs is_cache, path A vs path B), and the clean-upgrade contract (muted 'self-reported · AG-UI THINKING' chip reserves the SOLID 'observed intent' slot with zero layout change). leveragesMirageData (10): every surface is wired to a real return — getReplay+getSessionTrace, stamped tool_call_id join, the explicit JOIN IMPLEMENTATION NOTE that there is no /api/lineage so the touched-by is a client-side union of actions[] (matches reality exactly), and the warning to wire the debugger to /replay NOT the lossy useAgentStream reducer. This is the most data-faithful of the three. Learnability (8): a clear route table and a debugger metaphor most engineers already know from Redux DevTools; loses a point only because four regions + four-deep card disclosure + transport is real chrome (it mitigates with collapsible rail/inspector and Cmd-K escape). Buildability (9): the most directly implementable — concrete routes, exact inspector ASCII, exact lineage panel, reuses the shipped components verbatim, client-side fold of the pure _fold_replay_state. The risk list is the most honest and complete (heuristic fragility, touched-by scope, sampling, disabled-query-bar-looks-broken). My only deductions: the four-region density and the lens-as-pivot cognitive load are real for a first-timer.

The most faithful to how Snowsight ACTUALLY feels, and the one I'd be productive in fastest. The decisive idea — ONE persistent three-pane shell where the LEFT rail holds TWO trees, RUN HISTORY (top) and DATA CATALOG (bottom), side by side — is the single best structural move in the whole set: it makes the model-vs-data pivot a glance away because both worlds literally coexist in the rail, exactly like Snowsight keeping History and Databases persistent. Learnability (10): nothing to learn beyond 'open an object from the rail'; no dockable panes, no route-shuffle, one center that swaps object type. This is the lowest-friction product here and the most defensible 'it just works like Snowsight' pitch. Review-loop fit (9): history-as-gravity-well, lens strip over one cursor, Most-Expensive-Ops -> cursor, bidirectional open-in-Data / touched-by deep-links — all the right moves. Data View (9): table skin with stats strip, Schema+FK (labeled static), virtualized data.jsonl with per-column mini-profiles and click-to-filter, right-column column profile + pinned touched-by + ReservedMetadataStrip showing '—' on disk mounts (never zero-filled) — genuinely Snowsight-grade and honest. Loses nothing to Paradigm C on the table skin itself; I rate them equal here. Intent+command (8): excellent card spec with the same conservative INTENT≠EFFECT flag and clean-upgrade reserved slot; a touch less field-level precision than C's, but functionally equivalent. leveragesMirageData (9): correctly built on /replay + getSessionTrace + the client-side touched-by union, reuses all shipped components, honest about loaded-runs scope. Buildability (9): a single shell with a center object-swap is arguably SIMPLER to build than C's full router and certainly than B's dock grid; the two-tree rail + tight cross-links are the only place engineering must nail it. The chief risk it names itself — the two-tree rail + center swap can read as 'two apps bolted together' if cross-links aren't instant — is the one thing that could undercut its coherence, but the shared single-selection store (which the repo's consoleStore/sessionRunStore pattern supports) is the right mitigation. I rank it second only because Paradigm C's spec is marginally more build-ready and its Data View / lineage panel are described at a finer, less-ambiguous grain; on pure desirability for a Snowsight user these two are a coin-flip.

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — "The Workbench" (Paradigm B: IDE Workbench)
rankings.notes: The highest ceiling and the most genuinely powerful for a power user — and the riskiest. The cross-filter contract (one shared selection store; set opIdx anywhere and Inspector/State/Data/Lineage/Profile/transport all re-bind) is the soul of the idea and is exactly what I'd want when chasing a bug. The signature payoff — ⌘\ split to dock Time-Travel beside Profile over the SAME cursor, scrub on the left and watch Most-Expensive-Ops re-rank on the right — is the single most compelling power-user interaction in the entire set; no other design lets me see two lenses simultaneously. Data View (9): equal to the others — table skin, stats strip, disabled query bar, Schema/FK (labeled), data.jsonl with column profiles, touched-by both directions, dimmed graph preview. Intent+command (8): same strong card + conservative flag. leveragesMirageData (9): well-grounded, and it has the BEST risk self-awareness of the three — it explicitly calls out the getReplay fetch-storm and prescribes client-side fold (which I confirmed is valid: the endpoint returns full actions[] and _fold_replay_state is pure), and it correctly bans the lossy live stream from the correlation path. But two axes drag it down hard. Learnability (6): a freely splittable VS Code dock grid is intimidating versus 'open an object from the rail'; it knows this and ships Triage/Debug/Catalog presets + lens chips for the common swap-in-place path, but the danger that users never discover panes are dockable — or get lost arranging them — is real, and for a REVIEW tool (where the brief says reviewing > running) that overhead fights the mission. Buildability (6): a tab-and-split workbench with draggable dividers, per-workspace persisted layouts, and N panes all subscribing to one store is materially more engineering than a single center-swap (Snowsight) or a routed center (Paradigm C); none of the shipped components give you docking for free. It is the most expensive to build and the most expensive to learn, for a marginal-over-the-others gain on a review-centric product. The split-lenses-over-one-cursor idea, though, is too good to lose — it should be grafted as an OPTION onto the winner, not the default.

topPick: Mirage Console — Paradigm C: "The Trace Debugger" (effectively tied with the Snowsight Console at 54; C wins the tiebreak on spec-completeness and build-readiness)
bestIdeasToGraft: The TWO-TREE LEFT RAIL from the Snowsight Console — RUN HISTORY (top) + DATA CATALOG (bottom) persistently side by side — is the single best structural idea in the set. It makes the model-vs-data pivot a glance away because both worlds literally coexist in the rail. Adopt this as the shell instead of Paradigm C's left-rail-of-icons; it is more Snowsight-faithful and reduces navigation to 'open an object'.

The DOCKABLE SPLIT-LENS over ONE cursor from Paradigm B (⌘\ -> Time-Travel beside Profile, scrub left / watch Most-Expensive-Ops re-rank right). Do NOT make the whole app a dock grid; instead offer this as a single optional 'split lens' affordance for power users on top of the otherwise simple shell. It is the only way to see two lenses simultaneously and it is the genuine power-user payoff.

Paradigm C's field-level Data View + LINEAGE PANEL spec — the exact ASCII touched-by panel (group by run_id -> tool_call_id leaf, op-type/source facets, hop-2 co-touched line, the explicit 'op-level, this workspace's loaded runs, not a transitive provenance graph' footer, dimmed [graph ⤢] preview). This is the most honest and most build-ready lineage treatment; use it verbatim.

Paradigm C's discipline of showing TABLE-LEVEL stats.json SOLID next to MUTED client-derived per-column profiles, so authoritative engine-ish numbers are never confused with derived ones. This is exactly the distinction a Snowsight-literate user cares about and it should be a hard rule on the Data View.

Paradigm C's explicit JOIN IMPLEMENTATION NOTE + DATA WIRING NOTE (wire to /replay + getSessionTrace, NOT the lossy useAgentStream reducer which drops tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision; touched-by is a client-side union of actions[]). Bake these as architectural invariants — they are correct against the real code and prevent the two most likely correctness bugs.

Paradigm B's cross-filter fetch-storm mitigation: fetch full actions[] once per run, then fold stateAt(idx) CLIENT-SIDE for scrubbing (the server _fold_replay_state is pure and is the source of truth, so the client re-fold is provably identical). Apply to whichever design wins so scrubbing/skip-what-if is instant.

The conservative INTENT≠EFFECT flag with the clean-upgrade contract (muted 'self-reported · AG-UI THINKING' chip that flips to a SOLID 'observed intent' chip with zero layout change when a cognition plane lands), worded identically across all three — keep it exactly, including 'never fires when intent is absent' and the 'possible mismatch — heuristic, not a verdict' tooltip.

The persistent 'selected op' ANCHOR CHIP in the inspector header (Paradigm C) that never changes across lenses — the cheapest, most effective cure for the lens-as-pivot confusion that all three risk; pair it with a one-time coach-mark.
Cmd-K as the ONLY home for governance (Promote TEST->LIVE) — unanimous across all three. Keep promote demoted to a deliberate keystroke + a quiet branch chip; never a tempting button.
synthesisAdvice: Build ONE product = Snowsight Console's SHELL + Paradigm C's CONTENT, with Paradigm B's split-lens as an opt-in. Concretely: (1) Adopt the Snowsight Console's persistent three-pane shell and its TWO-TREE LEFT RAIL (Run History top, Data Catalog bottom) as the spine — this is the most learnable, most Snowsight-faithful frame and it solves the model-vs-data pivot structurally. Resist Paradigm B's freely-dockable VS Code grid as the default; it taxes learnability and buildability for a review-first tool. (2) Inside the center, use Paradigm C's debugger-organism for the Run view (LEFT spine of intent+command cards / CENTER lens-stage with the [PROFILE · TIME-TRAVEL · LINEAGE] segmented control over ONE cursor / RIGHT docked inspector with the persistent selected-op anchor chip / BOTTOM transport). Default lens = TIME-TRAVEL at cursor=last, DIFF tab open. (3) Use Paradigm C's Data View and lineage panel spec verbatim — it is the most complete and most honest; enforce the SOLID-stats.json vs MUTED-client-profile rule and the disabled query bar with NotImplementedError tooltip. (4) Graft Paradigm B's split-lens-over-one-cursor as a single optional 'split' affordance (⌘\\) for power users — NOT the default — so you get its payoff without its complexity. (5) Make the cross-link contract instant and bidirectional via one shared selection store ({workspaceId,branch,runId,opIdx,path}) backed by the existing consoleStore/sessionRunStore pattern; this is the make-or-break for the 'one shell, not two apps' feel that the Snowsight Console itself flags as its top risk. (6) Architecturally, hard-code Paradigm C's wiring invariants (build on /replay + getSessionTrace, never the lossy live reducer) and Paradigm B's fetch-storm fix (fetch actions[] once, fold client-side). (7) Carry the three honesty tiers as SHARED PRIMITIVES (border-style + text-opacity + chip), per Paradigm B's mitigation, so density never erodes the solid/muted/dimmed language — this is the whole credibility bet. (8) Keep the INTENT≠EFFECT flag conservative and the touched-by footer scope-honest ('this workspace's loaded runs, not an all-history index') on EVERY lineage surface. Net: the shell that's easiest to live in, wrapping the content that's most build-ready and most honest, with the one power-user superpower bolted on as an option.

judgePersona: Pragmatic eng lead grading buildability on the four real endpoints that exist today (/replay returning full actions[] + stateAt fold, the client-side touched-by join over mount_prefix+path, vfsList/vfsFile, getSessionTrace) versus aspirational surfaces, and weighting honest labeling of the solid/muted/dimmed tiers. I verified every load-bearing claim against the codebase before scoring.
topPick: Mirage Console — Paradigm C: "The Trace Debugger"

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — Paradigm C: "The Trace Debugger"
rankings.notes: Best buildability-honesty fit of the three. Every region maps to a verified endpoint with zero hand-waving: the four-region debugger reads getReplay(sessionId,cursor,run_id) which I confirmed returns the FULL actions[] plus the server stateAt fold (overlay/reads_so_far/cursor_op/diff) — so client re-fold scrubbing, skip-what-if, and the Most-Expensive-Ops rail are all derivations over data already in hand, no new endpoint. It is the ONLY design whose data-wiring note explicitly says 'wired exclusively to /replay + getSessionTrace; the live useAgentStream reducer drops tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision' — and that is literally true: the live VfsOp type in agui.ts carries only op/path/source/bytes/mount_prefix/duration_ms/timestamp, while ReplayAction carries the correlation fields. That correctness call alone saves a build from a silent correlation bug. The touched-by panel carries the exact honest scoping ('N runs loaded in THIS workspace, not an all-history index') with a JOIN IMPLEMENTATION NOTE that matches reality (no /api/lineage exists). Table skin is grounded in the real schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json fixtures (users 500 rows / 105,590 B confirmed) with a disabled query bar + NotImplementedError tooltip. The lens-as-pivot-on-one-cursor is the cleanest expression of the converged IA. Slight learnability cost: 4 regions + 4-deep card disclosure + bottom transport is dense, and 'switching lens keeps the same op' needs the coach-mark it proposes. Honest tier language is the most rigorous of the three (solid/muted/dimmed defined once as a literal visual treatment, reserved 'observed intent' slot upgrades with no layout change).

The most learnable and the strongest Data View of the three (the Table skin with FK row labeled 'declared schema, not observed dataflow', per-column client-side profiling, ReservedMetadataStrip showing '—' not zero-fill is the single best honesty detail in any design). The two-tree rail (Run History + Data Catalog always co-present) is the most immediately legible IA and the lowest-friction model-vs-data pivot. Loses buildability points for two reasons I weight heavily as the eng lead. (1) It NEVER names the live-stream footgun: it says the run/data cross-links are 'the identical VfsOp join read two ways' and references consoleStore/sessionRunStore, but unlike B/C it does not state that inspection must bind to /replay rather than the live reducer — a team could wire the Profile-tree leaf to the live VfsOp and silently lose tool_call_id/fingerprint, breaking the very cross-link the thesis rests on. (2) Its touched-by label is looser — 'cross-workspace-scoped to loaded runs' flirts with implying a cross-workspace index when the join is purely client-side over one workspace's loaded actions[]; B and C say 'this workspace's loaded runs' unambiguously. The 'no app-level routing, only the center swaps' shell is elegant but its own risk list admits it can read as two apps bolted together unless cross-links are instant; that's a real build risk for the central illusion. Everything else is impeccably grounded.

rankings.approach: Mirage Console — "The Workbench" (Paradigm B: IDE Workbench)
rankings.notes: Technically the most sophisticated and honest about its own data risks — its risk/mitigation list is the best of the three (names the cross-filter fetch storm and correctly prescribes client-side fold via porting _fold_replay_state since /replay returns full actions[]; names the live-stream lossiness; names touched-by overclaim; bakes honesty tiers into shared primitives). The cross-filter contract over one selection store is genuinely the same data spine as C, just arranged as dockable panes. But buildability and learnability both take real hits from the VS Code dock-grid itself: draggable/splittable panes with per-workspace localStorage layout persistence, drag dividers, dock presets, and 'split a lens right' Cmd-K verbs are a large amount of bespoke window-management UI to build and test BEFORE any mirage-specific value appears — and it is the most intimidating to a first-time reviewer (its own risk list concedes 'users may never discover panes are dockable'). For a READ-FIRST review console, the dock paradigm spends its complexity budget on chrome rather than on the model-vs-data question. The 3 presets mitigate but don't eliminate this. Same excellent Data View and intent+command grain as A/C, so it is not far behind on the substance — it's the shell cost that drops it.

(3) DATA VIEW: take A's Table skin wholesale, including the static-FK label, client-side column profiling caption, and the '—'-not-zero ReservedMetadataStrip. (4) HARD BUILD RULES, stated in the design doc and enforced in code: bind ALL inspection/correlation to /replay + getSessionTrace and treat the live stream as tail-only (verified: live VfsOp lacks tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision); re-fold stateAt(idx) client-side over the full actions[] that /replay already returns (port _fold_replay_state) and only re-fetch on run change to avoid a scrub fetch-storm; render the touched-by join client-side with the label 'in THIS workspace's loaded runs — not an all-history index' on EVERY panel, plus a 'load more runs to widen' affordance (use B's wording, not A's looser 'cross-workspace-scoped'). (5) HONESTY: define solid/muted/dimmed once as a shared primitive (border-style + opacity + ⓘ chip), never per-screen; never fabricate fingerprint/revision on disk mounts (omit); keep the INTENT≠EFFECT flag conservative and silent on absent intent. (6) LEARNABILITY: ship a one-time coach-mark on the 'lens keeps your selected op' behavior and lead with the swap-in-place lens control so the common path needs zero advanced-UI knowledge. Net: C's spine + A's data surface and rail + B's correctness mitigations = one coherent, fully-buildable, honestly-labeled page.
